c: I recently finished all nine seasons. Season one was so awkward that it took me several attempts to push through it. I kept hearing how good the show was, which kept me going. I gradually started liking it and ended up bingeing it. Seasons two, three, and four were the best. Michael Scott was ridiculous, but I could still understand him. He was less hateful and actually lovable. From season five until his departure, his personality felt increasingly scattered, less coherent, and less lovable. Meanwhile, I loved the other stories and the new CEOs. Andy Bernard becoming the office manager was unexpectedly interesting. I actually liked it, and I thought the final two seasons were pretty good. Most of the characters stayed consistent. Despite the rough start, this was one of the few series whose quality felt relatively consistent from the first season to the last.
